text:
## Observations

1. If the current pair is not `WA`, the search for the leftmost occurrence can advance one position.
2. Replacing `WA` with `AC` can create a new `WA` only one position to the left of the replacement.
3. Once the search reaches the end with no unchecked pair, the current string is the result.
4. Each replacement removes one `W` and introduces none, so there are at most as many replacements as characters.

## Solution sketch

> If the current pair is not `WA`, the search for the leftmost occurrence can advance one position.

1. Read the string into a mutable list of characters. Start at the first position and examine each adjacent pair. If it is not `WA`, advance one position. Throughout the scan, every pair starting before the current position has already been ruled out.

> Replacing `WA` with `AC` can create a new `WA` only one position to the left of the replacement.

2. When the current pair is `WA`, it is the leftmost occurrence, so overwrite it with `AC`. The new pair at that position is `AC`, and the pair immediately to its right, if present, starts with `C`. Only the pair immediately to the left could now be `WA`. Move back one position to check it, staying at the first position if the replacement was there.

> Once the search reaches the end with no unchecked pair, the current string is the result.

3. Stop when the current position has no character to its right. Join the characters and print the result. A one-character string has no pairs to examine, and a string without `WA` passes through the scan unchanged.

> Each replacement removes one `W` and introduces none, so there are at most as many replacements as characters.

4. For a string of length \(n\), each of the at most \(n\) replacements adds at most one backward move. The forward moves cover the length of the string plus the positions revisited after those backward moves. The total time is \(O(n)\), and the character list uses \(O(n)\) space.

generation.note: Harness wall time includes Codex startup; not API latency.

usage.note: Codex token counts include its harness context; not comparable to API usage.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
